name: NE Edge Millstone Data Center
additional_info: Two 2-story hyperscale data centers on 25 acres of Dominion Energy's Millstone Nuclear Power Station property. Building 1: 1.14M sqft; Building 2: 428K sqft. Direct "behind the meter" 300 MW connection to Millstone Reactors 2 and 3. Host fee agreement signed March 2023 with Town of Waterford ($231M over 30 years in lieu of property taxes). CT Siting Council denied key petition (January 2024). Building permit deadline clause in host fee agreement required permits by March 2026 — deadline appears to have lapsed. Developer George McLaughlin III. Strong community opposition (Concerned Citizens of Waterford). CT Legislature passed bill requiring ISO-NE study of grid impact (2024). Behind-the-meter design means project bypasses ISO-NE queue. Immersion cooling; no water consumption design. Project deemed On Hold as permit deadline passed without permit issuance. Host Fee Agreement ended due to default and expired per its terms (CT Mirror, April 2026). Project now Cancelled.
source: CT Mirror (2024-01-19) | CT Mirror (2026-04-15) | Data Center Dynamics (2023-02-22) | Cleanview (2026-05)
address: Millstone Power Station, Rope Ferry Road, Waterford, CT 06385
transmission_upgrades.description: Behind-the-meter design — direct connection to Millstone nuclear plant bypassing ISO-NE grid.

name: GotSpace Groton Campus
additional_info: Two 250,000 sqft data centers in Groton. GotSpace (related to NE Edge co-founder Quinn). Town of Groton Planning and Zoning Commission enacted 1-year moratorium on large data centers (2024). Town officials ceased discussions. Subject to $30B lawsuit from GotSpace. MW not publicly disclosed.

name: GotSpace Bozrah Campus
additional_info: 980,000 sqft single building. Developer: GotSpace. Same developer as Groton campus. Under moratorium cloud. MW not publicly disclosed.

name: Atlas Capital Group CT Data Center
additional_info: Cleanview shows project in Hartford, CT. No public MW or address confirmed. Developer details not publicly disclosed as of May 2026.

name: NEMA Data Center (ISO-NE Study Project)
additional_info: Listed in ISO-NE Load Forecast Committee presentation (March 27, 2026) as the only data center project in formal ISO-NE study as of CELT 2026. 200 MW nameplate (prior to derating). Timeline: through 2027. Location: NEMA load zone (Northeast Massachusetts). Developer identity not disclosed. Not yet under construction; excluded from summer 2026 and winter 2026/2027 peak forecasts. Expected to begin affecting forecasts from winter 2027/2028 onward.

name: Servistar Westfield Data Center Campus
additional_info: 120-acre campus; 10 three-story buildings planned; 2.7M sqft total over 13-18 years. Local approval 2021; PILOT tax agreement. 2024 MA sales/use tax exemption for data centers was key catalyst. Westmass Area Development Corp CEO Jeff Daley said Aug 2025 pre-development could begin within 6 months. However, Dec 2025 investigation by The Shoestring found Daley declined interview, saying Westmass "is not under contract at the moment." Developer appears to have stalled or departed the project without signing a tenant. No hyperscale anchor tenant identified. Construction has not begun. Eversource substation and transmission interconnect in place. MW load not publicly stated (no signed tenant). Project classified On Hold pending tenant identification. [Stage updated 2026-08-24: The City reported that the locally approved project is again being evaluated and that the applicant submitted a technical fact sheet covering cooling technology, anticipated water use, and electrical-service plans.]
source: The Shoestring (2025-12-30) | NBC Boston (2025-08-22) | Baxtel | City of Westfield (2026-06-15)

name: JGT2 / Sentinel Data Centers Jay Mill
developer: JGT2 Redevelopment LLC / Sentinel Data Centers
additional_info: Redevelopment of former Androscoggin Mill (closed 2023 after Pixelle Specialty Solutions departure following 2020 boiler explosion). 1 million sqft on two floors. Tenant: Sentinel Data Centers. Developer: JGT2 Redevelopment LLC (Tony McDonald, Boulos Company). 82 MW initial demand with potential to scale. 150 MW solar on-site (replaces existing gas turbine) — does NOT require grid upgrades per developer. No local approval needed under current Jay land use policies. $550M valuation. $6M+ annual property tax projected. Governor Mills cited Jay project as reason for vetoing LD 307 (April 24, 2026). Veto sustained by legislature. Path now clear for permitting. [Stage updated 2026-08-24: Sentinel Data Centers told site owner JGT2 Redevelopment that it did not intend to proceed with the former Androscoggin Mill project. JGT2 is seeking other interested parties, but the data center project is currently on hold.]
source: Portland Press Herald (2026-03-13) | Sun Journal (2026-03-25) | Governor Mills Veto Letter (2026-04-24) | Maine Monitor (2026-03-25) | Data Center Dynamics (2026-06-12)

name: Loring LiquidCool Data Center
additional_info: Phase 1: 5-6 MW. Full potential: up to 50 MW. 115,000 sqft in building 7230 (former warehouse). Immersion cooling technology using polyalphaolefin oil. No water consumption; no noise. Powered partly by New Brunswick hydropower. Green 4 Maine LLC (owner of 450-acre former base campus) signed long-term lease with LiquidCool Solutions (Rochester, MN). Maine's first AI-focused large data center. "Three-Ring Binder" fiber directly on campus. Announced October 2025; expected operational within 6 months of announcement. Additional data centers planned for campus.
source: Bangor Daily News (2025-10-14) | WABI (2025-10-17) | Portland Press Herald (2025-10-15)
address: Building 7230, Former Loring Air Force Base, Limestone, ME 04750

name: Loring LiquidCool Data Center Expansion
additional_info: Planned expansion phases after Phase 1. Full campus potential up to 50 MW. Additional facilities expected at Green 4 Maine campus. Timeline not confirmed.

name: Northern New England Energy Co. Sanford Data Center
additional_info: Developer: Northern New England Energy Company (parent company not publicly named). 100-300 MW capacity (200 MW midpoint used). Land purchased. Well into planning; met with local officials and Maine Dept. of Energy Resources. Behind-the-meter: fuel cells + solar + battery storage — generates all own electricity. Sanford Water District has confirmed unused capacity (300,000-500,000 gallons/day demand). 100 long-term jobs. First disclosed Feb 2026 by Sen. Matt Harrington (R-Sanford) at LD 307 work session. Cited LD 307 moratorium as existential threat; project proceeded after veto was sustained. Developer identity not publicly confirmed beyond "Northern New England Energy Company."
source: Data Center Dynamics (2026-03-11) | Maine Public (2026-02-16) | Portland Press Herald (2026-02-18) | The Maine Wire (2026-02-20)
address: Sanford, York County, ME (approx. 35 miles SW of Portland)

name: Unknown Developer Wiscasset Data Center
additional_info: 300-acre hyperscale proposal. Developer operating under NDA — identity undisclosed. $5 billion project. Wiscasset town officials voted November 4, 2025, to pause data center discussion after community backlash. Status: On Hold pending outcome of statewide policy process and community engagement. Substation and transmission lines visible near site. NDA means no public developer confirmation.
address: Old Ferry Road, Wiscasset, Lincoln County, ME (adjacent to former Maine Yankee Atomic Energy Plant site)

name: Eastport Underwater AI Data Center
additional_info: Needham, MA-based developer proposing submerged AI data centers off Eastport coast. Eastport city has 14 full-time employees and a 2026 legal budget of $10,000 — essentially no capacity to engage a major permitting process. Local opposition citing city fiscal strain. Very early/speculative. No MW, investment, or timeline confirmed. Developer not publicly named.
address: Offshore Eastport, Washington County, ME (easternmost city in US)

name: NE Edge Killingly Data Center
additional_info: Land purchased by NE Edge LLC from Town of Killingly for $5M (August 8, 2023). Three parcels including 125 Alexander Parkway and two adjacent lots. Developer: NE Edge LLC (George McLaughlin III). MW not publicly disclosed. NE Edge was previously unsuccessful with Groton and Bozrah CT proposals, and the Waterford Millstone project was cancelled April 2026. Status of Killingly project as of May 2026 unclear given developer setbacks.

name: O&G Industries Beacon Falls Data Center
additional_info: O&G Industries (Connecticut construction and materials company) received approval for a 32 MW data center in Beacon Falls in 2022. Timeline and current construction status not confirmed as of May 2026. [Stage updated 2026-08-24: O&G is exploring a revised fuel-cell-powered data center at the same Lopus Road site. The newly reported concept is 100 MW, replacing the prior 32 MW version that did not materialize.]
address: Beacon Falls, New Haven County, CT

name: Proposed Lewiston Data Center (Bates Mill)
additional_info: 24 MW proposed at former Bates Mill 3 complex in downtown Lewiston. Lewiston City Council voted against the project in late December 2025 after swift community opposition — concerns about electricity prices, environmental impact, and downtown location near residential areas. Developer not publicly named.
address: Former Bates Mill Complex, Lewiston, Androscoggin County, ME

name: Moulton Nottingham Data Center
additional_info: Concept-stage AI data center proposed on a 100-plus-acre Old Turnpike Road property, with approximately 40 acres contemplated for development. The developer withdrew the May planning-board application following local opposition; subsequent reporting said he was considering reintroduction.
